item.title: Govt plans two-part budget session in 2026
item.description: Jammu: The budget session of the Jammu & Kashmir Legislative Assembly is likely to be held in two parts- the first before the holy month of Ramadhan and the second after Eid-ul-Fitr, sources said. As per reports the NC-led government is considering holding the budget session in two phases. “If all goes as per plan, the first part of the session will be held before the beginning of the holy month of Ramadhan. item.title: Centre raises excise duty on cigarettes; new rates to take effect from February 1.
item.description: Srinagar,Jan 1: The Finance Ministry has notified a major revision in excise duty on cigarettes and other tobacco products, with the new rates set to come into effect from February 1, 2026. According to the official notification, the government has imposed an additional excise duty on cigarettes ranging from Rs 2,050 to Rs 8,500 per 1,000 sticks. item.title: Leh Freezes at –10.6°C as Sub-Zero Cold Tightens Grip on Kashmir
item.description: Srinagar,Jan 3 : Cold conditions continued across Kashmir and Ladakh on Saturday, with large parts of the Valley recording sub-zero night temperatures, while Ladakh remained in the grip of intense cold, officials said. In Ladakh, temperatures stayed well below the freezing point, with Leh recording a minimum of minus 10.6 degrees Celsius. item.description: Srinagar,Jan 3: Jammu Police conducted a routine checking drive as part of its continued efforts to enforce food safety norms and safeguard public health, officials said. item.title: Missing Woman traced by Kulgam Police, reunited with Family
item.description: Kulgam, Jan 3 : Police in South Kashmir’s Kulgam have traced a woman who had gone missing on November 17, 2025, and reunited her with her family after sustained efforts and coordinated investigation. Officials said that on November 26, 2025, Police Station Kulgam received a written complaint from Waseem Ahmad Wani, stating that his wife, Bisma Jan, was missing from her rented accommodation at Amnoo area of Kulgam since November 17. item.title: Gulmarg records –8.8°C as severe cold deepens across Kashmir
item.description: Srinagar,Jan 5: Gulmarg witnessed the coldest night of the season so far, with temperatures plunging to minus 8.8 degrees Celsius. Across the Kashmir Valley, Srinagar recorded a minimum temperature of minus 3.6 degrees Celsius, with similar readings at the Srinagar airport. Pahalgam and Shopian experienced lows of minus 4.8 and minus 5.6 degrees Celsius respectively, while Pulwama recorded minus 4.2 degrees Celsius.
